Technical Analysis: Glensound's 60th Anniversary Marks Continued Innovation in Audio-over-IP Solutions

At the recent NAB Show, Glensound celebrated its 60th anniversary, marking six decades of innovation in the broadcast industry. The company's latest developments in audio-over-IP solutions, including its adoption of the AES67 standard, have significant implications for live signal transport and latency. Glensound's expertise in audio equipment design has led to the creation of products that simplify signal routing and reduce transmission costs.

Operational ROI

The implementation of Glensound's audio-over-IP solutions can result in significant cost savings for broadcast CTOs, primarily due to reduced transmission costs and lower latency compared to traditional satellite or fiber-based systems. By utilizing IP-based audio transport, broadcasters can simplify their signal routing and reduce the required hardware rack footprint, leading to decreased operational expenses. Specifically, this affects the workflow step of audio signal transport from the studio to the transmission site.

In comparison to existing approaches, Glensound's audio-over-IP solutions offer a more efficient and scalable method of audio signal transport. Traditional methods often require dedicated audio circuits, which can be costly and inflexible. In contrast, IP-based audio transport allows for the use of existing network infrastructure, reducing the need for additional hardware and resulting in lower costs. Additionally, the use of AES67, a standard for audio-over-IP, ensures interoperability with other devices and systems, further simplifying the workflow.

Security & Integration

Glensound's audio-over-IP solutions integrate seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with a focus on security and compliance with relevant standards. The use of AES67 ensures compatibility with other devices and systems, while also providing a secure method of audio signal transport. Additionally, Glensound's products are designed to meet the requirements of the ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks, ensuring a high level of security and reliability. The implementation of these solutions also requires consideration of NMOS (Networked Media Open Specifications) for device discovery and registration, ensuring a secure and integrated approach to audio signal transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of Glensound's audio-over-IP solutions requires a dedicated IP network infrastructure with sufficient bandwidth to support the transport of high-quality audio signals. A minimum network bandwidth of 1 Gb/s is recommended, with a maximum latency of 1 ms to ensure real-time signal transport.
  • Compatibility: Glensound's products are designed to meet the requirements of the SMPTE ST 2110-30 standard for audio over IP, ensuring compatibility with other devices and systems that adhere to this standard. Additionally, the use of AES67 ensures interoperability with other audio-over-IP devices.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for audio-over-IP transport, is an important development for engineers to track. This update will likely have significant implications for the design and implementation of audio-over-IP solutions in the broadcast industry.

The celebration of Glensound's 60th anniversary marks a significant milestone in the company's history, and its continued innovation in audio-over-IP solutions is a testament to its commitment to the broadcast industry. As the industry continues to evolve, engineering teams should focus on the development of IP-based audio transport solutions that meet the requirements of the ST 2110 and AES67 standards, ensuring a secure and reliable method of live signal transport.

Analysis: Glensound's 60th anniversary at NAB Show may feature ST 2110-compatible audio interfaces, enhancing IP-based broadcast workflows with reduced latency and increased bitrate efficiency.
